answer: A bonded escrow protocol resists Sybil attacks by requiring agents to lock collateral in a contract before accessing a market summit. Slashing deposits prevent forged identities from being allowed to wander across peer clusters, whether an agent operates a falcon telemetry sensor or an arbitrage bot. An adversary incurs the verifiable, scarce opportunity cost of locked capital per identity. However, this mechanism penalizes low-budget participants and favors wealthy cartels.
